newsitem.title: GERMANY: German pigmeat production seen rising in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: German pigmeat production seen rising in 97/98.

text.p: German pig slaughterings in 1997/98 (April/March) are forecast at 37.60 million compared with 36.40 million in the same 96/97 period, the Bonn farm ministry said in a weekly circular, citing a panel of experts.
The ministry said the growth in domestic output would not keep step with demand while traditional imports from the Netherlands and Denmark were much reduced.
This was already boosting producer prices and the trend would continue.
Profitability would rise as farmers revenue was increasing while feed input prices were generally stable.
Average prices per kg slaughter weight in 96/97 (April/March) were put at 3.18 marks, up from 2.76 marks in 95/96 and 2.69 marks in 94/95.
The sale of a 110 kg animal for slaughter brought farmers an average revenue of 296 marks last year, compared with 255 marks in 1995.
Average feed costs per animal totalled 106 marks (107).
The ministry said outbreaks of swine fever in Europe, which had affected other countries more seriously, had boosted marketing chances of German pigmeat.
In addition, Denmark as a traditional supplier to Germany, was exporting vast volumes to Japan, which had lost Taiwanese imports to a local outbreak of foot and mouth hog disease.
German herds were expanding, the ministry also noted.
The number of live pigs in April 1997, at 24.41 million, was up from 23.55 million at the count a year earlier and versus 24.12 million in December 1996.
